factual_methodology.summary: Two material scope/measurement errors remain in both editions. First, the ECDC value of 3.75 per 100,000, the +72% change and the 2.07 target are explicitly the estimated total EU incidence, not EU/EEA incidence; the current prose and EN/PT-BR table label them EU/EEA. Second, the ANIMUSE 83,254-tonne figure is reported quantities of antimicrobial agents intended for use in animals, based primarily on sales and imports; the current sentence says the agents 'were used'/'foram utilizadas', implying administered use despite the report's explicit distinction between market-level data and farm-level administration.

evidence_traceability.summary: The opening paragraph attaches references [4][5] to the 2026 Global Action Plan and the 2024 UN Political Declaration. Reference [4] is the ECDC ESAC-Net consumption report and does not support either claim; [5] is the WHO Global Action Plan release; [6] is the UN declaration but is never cited. References [6]–[10] are all absent from body citations, while producer_checks.source_audit reports ten references. In addition, the 9% increase among 74 participants is attributed to the ANIMUSE interactive report, although the WOAH PDF itself presents that separate 2018–2024 analysis in its executive summary and Chapter 4.

contrary_evidence: Among 80 consistent WOAH participants, the biomass-adjusted indicator declined 3% from 2019 to 2024 (108 to 105 mg/kg).
A separate WOAH analysis of 74 participants found a 9% increase over 2018–2024; the cohorts and periods differ and should not be merged.
EU/EEA antimicrobial consumption fell 5% from the 2019 baseline in 2025 and the Access share increased, although both 2030 targets remain unmet.
The WHO and ECDC reports show expanded national plans and surveillance coverage alongside substantial implementation and diagnostic gaps.
limitations: ANIMUSE quantitative estimates rely primarily on sales/import and other market-level data; only five of 119 participants selected farm records as a validated quantitative source.
The WOAH 2024 biomass-normalized indicator excludes companion animals and uses estimated terrestrial and aquatic food-producing animal biomass.
The 2025 growth-promotion questionnaire describes the situation when the eleventh round launched in 2025 and is not the same observation year as the 2024 quantitative-use data.
The ECDC country-threshold results use invasive isolates and country-level combinations; they are not community prevalence or the proportion of all infections.
The report does not establish a causal link between the animal-use indicators and the human clinical resistance patterns presented; the datasets are distinct and should remain analytically separate.
The 9% trend analysis is in the WOAH report itself; the current sentence incorrectly attributes it to the interactive report.
The latest public build is blocked by an unrelated existing report defect; approval is not granted and no deployment is claimed.

locations: en.md:13 — paragraph ending '[4][5]' after the 2026 Global Action Plan and 2024 UN Political Declaration
issues.evidence: Reference [4] is the ECDC ESAC-Net 2025 antimicrobial-consumption report; [5] is the WHO 2026–2036 Global Action Plan release; [6] is the UN General Assembly Political Declaration A/RES/79/2. The paragraph's two policy claims are not supported by [4], and the direct UN declaration reference [6] is not cited. References [6]–[10] are not cited anywhere in either body, while the pending source_audit counts all ten as references. The WOAH report itself records the 2024 UN commitment to meaningfully reduce antimicrobial use in agrifood systems by 2030 (ANIMUSE Global Report, Chapter 4, pp. 44–45).
issues.required_correction: In both editions, cite [5] for the 2026 Global Action Plan and [6] for the 2024 UN Political Declaration (for example, replace the opening '[4][5]' with '[5][6]'). Add inline citations for references [7]–[10] only where each directly supports a specific claim, or remove unused entries and renumber the bibliography consistently. Recompute producer_checks.source_audit from sources actually cited; do not count unused URLs as evidence.
